key_insight: Synthetic data is only worth adding when it improves coverage of target-relevant directions faster than it introduces training errors, and that value changes with the current training set.
engineering_relevance: For LLM fine-tuning, TATC offers a principled way to choose synthetic examples that should improve downstream task performance without blindly increasing dataset size.
method: Derive a linear theory for when synthetic examples are useful, how much to add, and the marginal value of each new example.
Use Training-Aware Target Coverage (TATC) to rank candidates by beneficial training effect and target-direction coverage.
Select synthetic data that expands underrepresented target-relevant directions while filtering harmful examples.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that experiments on text and image data support the theory, and on GSM8K TATC improves synthetic selection for fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct across selection budgets.
watch_item: The approach depends on a linear approximation, so its guidance may weaken when training dynamics or synthetic errors are strongly nonlinear.
paper_title: Training-Aware Target Coverage for Synthetic Data Selection
